nodes.definition: A citable paper, report, standard, or other document that supplies provenance.
An author, contributor, expert, or responsible individual.
An institution, utility, regulator, company, or research group.
An exact sentence, paragraph, table cell, caption, or other source fragment grounding an extraction.
A specific phrase occurrence that may refer to a canonical ontology entity.
A benchmark, monitoring series, experimental dataset, or curated corpus.
The original database, sensor, monitoring program, or document collection from which data were obtained.
A bounded laboratory, pilot, full-scale, computational, or evaluation activity.
A measured, calculated, predicted, or extracted result under stated conditions.
A source-supported proposition, conclusion, comparison, or recommendation.
A named AI framework, agentic system, or decision-support platform.
A language, machine-learning, graph, statistical, hydraulic, or process model.
A role-bearing autonomous or semi-autonomous component of an AI system.
An external solver, simulator, database interface, API, or execution tool.
An analytical, experimental, optimization, retrieval, or modeling method.
A research, analytical, operational, or decision objective.
A versioned codebase, package, repository, script, executable, or model checkpoint.
A human-managed system for abstraction, treatment, distribution, collection, reuse, or discharge of water.
The origin from which water is abstracted or received by an engineered system.
The water or aqueous medium in which a measurement, treatment, or exposure occurs.
A facility that performs one or more water or wastewater treatment processes.
An ordered sequence of treatment units or processes.
A physical unit operation or reactor within a treatment train.
A physical, chemical, or biological process used to alter water quality.
A chemical, biological, particulate, or radiological constituent of concern.
A microbial taxon, functional group, pathogen, or treatment-community member.
A discrete or composite quantity of water, sludge, residual, or biomass collected for analysis.
A time- and location-bounded event during which one or more samples were collected.
A sludge, concentrate, brine, spent media, or other residual generated by treatment.
A deliberate operational, infrastructure, chemical, or control change evaluated in a water system.
A named configurable or observed value defining a system, process, experiment, or model setting.
A scientific, operational, economic, or AI evaluation measure.
An experimental, environmental, spatial, temporal, or operating context.
A geographic, administrative, site-level, or sampling location.
A limitation, risk, uncertainty, requirement, or knowledge gap.
An environmental, health, economic, or social outcome associated with a water-system decision.
A regulation, guideline, permit limit, or technical standard governing water systems or measurements.
A clear scientific, environmental, technical, or societal concept used to connect findings across publications.
A natural or anthropogenic environmental process that changes matter, energy, organisms, or environmental conditions.
A physical environmental medium or compartment in which substances, organisms, or processes occur.
A natural or engineered material, medium, adsorbent, membrane, catalyst, or construction substance.
A chemical element, compound, mixture, reagent, or additive whether or not it is considered a contaminant.
An organism, biological community, gene, protein, tissue, or other biological entity not limited to microorganisms.
A causal, physical, chemical, biological, or computational mechanism explaining how a process or outcome occurs.
A general or named technology, technical platform, or technological approach that is broader than a specific tool or treatment unit.
A policy, strategy, program, or governance instrument that guides decisions but is not necessarily a binding standard.
A material, energy, financial, informational, land, or water resource consumed, conserved, recovered, or managed.
A named physical, chemical, biological, environmental, or technical property of an entity or system.

relationships.definition: Connects a publication to an author.
Connects a person to an organization.
Records a citation between publications.
Links a document to an exact evidence fragment.
Links a fragment to a phrase occurrence.
Maps a mention to a canonical entity without erasing the mention.
Grounds a result or claim in exact source evidence.
Links a publication to a result it reports.
Links a publication to a bounded study activity.
Identifies outputs of an experiment or computational evaluation.
Links a claim to supporting evidence.
Links claims that conflict within a defined scope.
Records provenance of data or results.
Identifies the principal subject of a result or claim.
Identifies the metric represented by an observation.
Identifies the sample or matrix in which an observation applies.
Identifies how an observation was generated.
Attaches governing conditions or settings.
Identifies the physical sampling point.
Links a sample to its collection event.
Specifies the water or residual matrix.
Places infrastructure inside a managed water system.
Links a plant to an ordered treatment train.
Links a treatment train to one of its physical units.
Identifies the process performed by a physical treatment unit.
Represents treatment-train order.
Represents water flow into a plant or unit.
Represents directed water flow between units or to discharge/reuse.
States that a process or unit treats a water matrix or chemical substance.
Identifies the intended target of treatment or intervention.
States that removal was evaluated; magnitude belongs on an Observation.
Represents chemical or biological transformation.
Links treatment to a generated residual stream.
Links a study or system to a deliberate change.
Represents a sentence-supported influence on scientific, environmental, technical, biological, resource, or system outcomes.
Represents an explicitly supported causal relationship across water-domain and cross-domain concepts.
Links a system component to an energy-use observation.
Links a system or process to an emitted substance or quantified emission.
Provides spatial context.
Links systems or results to applicable requirements.
Records a reported limitation or risk.
Links a publication to a contribution it introduces.
Links an AI system to a component agent.
Links a system or agent to an underlying model.
Links a workflow component to an external implementation tool.
Links a study or system to a dataset.
Links a study, system, or experiment to a method.
Identifies a task performed.
Links a model to a predicted result or target metric.
Identifies the variable, objective, or system optimized.
Identifies evaluation data or experiment.
Identifies an evaluation measure.
Represents a source-supported comparative result.
